lines: Statim reaches 68 decisions per second on an RTX 3070.
Laya needs a Python stack and huge memory, but Statim uses just a small binary.
Statim is a native C++20 engine for System-1 decision models compatible with Laya and Jev, built for clients switching from Python.
Each adapter owns its adapted weights so latency stays low without merging, and each row of results confirms this behavior.
Type a question and get billing or urgency scores back instantly.
On S1Bench, the multilingual model scores 0.638 macro accuracy above its untuned Laya base on a public suite of 3,880 items.
Statim uses a 5.5 MB binary while ONNX Runtime needs 579 to 581 MiB at startup.
The native C++ tokenizer is identical on 3,906 cases and about 10 times faster.
Run it on Linux x86-64 with AVX2, or use Vulkan for GPU acceleration.
Apache-2.0 licence, one GitHub star, and tested on real hardware.
Run this curl command to download the binary, then verify it with sha256sum.
Save this for when you need a small binary instead of a Python stack.
Statim is a small C++ engine ready for you now.

log.say: Statim reaches 1,683 milliseconds per English state on CPU, while ONNX Runtime takes 1,683 milliseconds per state.
log.receipt:
| Measure | **Statim** | **ORT** |
| Short inputs, f32, 8 threads, ms per state | **257** | 266 |
| 1,024 tokens, f32, 8 threads, ms | **4,399** | 11,421 |
| Short inputs, f32, 16 threads (SMT), ms per state | 457 | **366** |
| First answer after process start, f32 | **0.45 s** | 2.06 s |
| Resident memory at start-up, 8-bit | **276 MiB** | 579–581 MiB |
|... 
### GPU performance
GPU build and launch instructions are in docs/BUILD.md.
| Path | CPU | RTX 3070 | Gain |
| Multilingual state | 535 ms | **54 ms** | ~10× |
| English state | 1,683 ms | **137 ms** | ~12× |
| Multilingual rate1 client | 2.68 req/s | **20.5 req/s** | 7.7× |
| Multilingual p501 client | 353 ms | **45 ms** | — |
| English rate1 client | 0.91 req/s | **8.1 req/s** | 8.9× |
|... 
```
